core.label: Core readiness
core.description: Essential public project foundations that most open-source repositories should address.

maturity.label: Operational maturity
maturity.description: Deeper practices that help a project operate safely, accessibly, transparently, and sustainably.

items.title: Repository includes a clear open-source license
items.description: Add a recognized open-source license in the repository root and explain its coverage clearly.

items.title: Repository includes a Code of Conduct
items.description: Publish community behavior expectations and make private reporting and enforcement information easy to find.

items.title: README explains the project clearly
items.description: Explain what the software does, who it helps, how to use it, and how people can participate.

items.title: Contributing guide is available
items.description: Add beginner-friendly steps for reporting issues, proposing changes, testing, and submitting pull requests.

items.title: Changelog tracks important updates
items.description: Document notable changes so users and contributors can follow the project's release history.

items.title: Roadmap shows planned improvements
items.description: Publish current priorities and distinguish shipped work from planned or deferred ideas.

items.title: Issue tracker is linked and welcoming
items.description: Make it easy to report bugs, suggest focused improvements, and find work suitable for new contributors.

items.title: Security policy explains responsible reporting
items.description: Document supported versions, security scope, and a private route for reporting sensitive concerns.

items.title: Decision-making and maintainer roles are documented
items.description: Explain who maintains the project, how decisions are made, and how roles and responsibilities may change.

items.title: Project site supports the software community
items.description: Provide documentation, releases, roadmap details, contribution routes, and project policies directly related to the software.

items.title: Accessibility commitment and reporting process are published
items.description: State the project's accessibility goal, current limitations, supported environments, and how barriers can be reported.

items.title: Automated and human accessibility verification is documented
items.description: Combine automated evidence with keyboard, screen-reader, zoom, reflow, contrast, motion, and device testing appropriate to the project.

items.title: Code of Conduct reporting and enforcement are operational
items.description: Define private reporting, conflict handling, evidence protection, proportionate consequences, anti-retaliation, and review options.

items.title: Sensitive vulnerabilities can be reported privately
items.description: Provide a verified private channel, realistic acknowledgement expectations, and coordinated disclosure guidance.

items.title: Project assets, trust boundaries, and misuse cases are reviewed
items.description: Maintain a lightweight threat model that reflects the architecture, likely abuse cases, mitigations, residual risks, and review triggers.

items.title: Security incident response is documented
items.description: Define how incidents are received, triaged, contained, remediated, verified, disclosed, and reviewed afterward.

items.title: Contributor pathways support first and repeat participation
items.description: Offer focused entry points, explain review expectations, recognize non-code work, and show how trusted responsibilities may grow.

items.title: Support scope and maintainer availability are documented
items.description: Explain supported request types, realistic response expectations, out-of-scope work, triage outcomes, and maintainer breaks.

items.title: Temporary absence, succession, and project transfer are planned
items.description: Document how responsibilities and service access will be protected when maintainers pause, step down, or transfer stewardship.

items.title: Project-health metrics are connected to goals and privacy
items.description: Define a small set of useful repository and community measurements without treating popularity as health or adding invasive tracking.

items.title: Dependency, documentation, and asset licensing are reviewed
items.description: Confirm that third-party code, actions, images, documentation, and other assets have compatible terms and required attribution.

items.title: Repository and release access follow least privilege
items.description: Protect important branches and services, require appropriate review, use strong account security, and document permission criteria.
